summary: Arthur Waley was a scholar in Sinology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who attended Rugby School and King's College, also studying under Gustav Haloun. He held posts at the British Museum (1913) and SOAS University of London (~1929–1930).
Aruna Haldar is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Kedar Nath Ojha and Girindrasekhar Bose. She held a teaching post at Patna University.

Arunoday Natvarlal Jani was an Indology scholar who studied under M. V. Upadhyay and earned his Ph.D. from the University of Mumbai under Govindlal Hargovind Bhatt in 1953. He was attested as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit at Baroda College in 1957.

Arvind Sharma works in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, having studied at the University of Allahabad, Syracuse, Harvard Divinity School, and Harvard University. He held posts at the University of Queensland (~1976–1980), McGill University (~1987), and Harvard University.

Asanga Tilakaratne is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who served as Professor and Head of Buddhist Philosophy at the University of Kelaniya's Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, where he was attested as department head (1993) and professor (2006).
Asatoshi Kamiya, a Buddhist studies scholar, earned an M.A. from Komazawa University. Kamiya was attested as a teacher at Mejiro Kenshin Junior and Senior High School in 1978.
Asef Bayat studied at the University of Kent (~1980–1984). He held posts at Leiden University (2000–2010) and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (~2010).
Asen Balikci studied at Columbia University (~1957–1962) and held a post at Université de Montréal (~1960–1994).

Ashby Butnor specializes in philosophy and Japanology, completing a PhD at the University of Hawaii under Vrinda Dalmiya in 2009. Butnor was attested as a Visiting Assistant Professor at Metropolitan State University of Denver in 2011.

Ashok Aklujkar is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who studied at Savitribai Phule Pune University and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. He served as a professor at the University of British Columbia (~1969–2006).
Ashok Kumar Malhotra is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at the East-West Center (~1964–1969). He founded the State University of New York at Oneonta.
Ashok Vajpeyi is an Indology scholar who completed his studies, including an MA, at St. Stephen's College, Delhi (~1961–1963).

Asim Kumar Chatterjee is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who earned a Ph.D. under D. Mukherjee at the University of Calcutta in 1967. He served as a lecturer at Jangipur College and Senior Research Fellow at Calcutta (attested 1970).

Asko Parpola is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Pentti Aalto, R. Panneerselvam, and P. R. Subramanian. He held posts at the Nordic Institute of Asian Studies, Academy of Finland, and the University of Helsinki (~1982–2004).

Asutosh Mookerjee was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology who studied at South Suburban School, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta. He held posts at Calcutta High Court (1904) and served as President at the University of Calcutta (1906–1914, 1921–1923).
Atsuhiko Yoshida is a religious studies and linguistics scholar who studied at Seikei University and the University of Tokyo (~1953–1957). He held a post at Seikei University (~1968–1999).
Atsushi Ibuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University (~1978–1987). Ibuki held a professorship at Toyo University (~2005).

Atsushi Kanazawa is a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1971–1983). He taught at the Meteorological College (~1985–1994) and served as an associate professor and professor at Komazawa University (~1995–2006).
Atsushi Kiyozawa is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Delhi. Kiyozawa was attested as a lecturer at Kindai University in 1989.

Atsushi Uno is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Kyoto University and Banaras Hindu University under T. R. V. Murti. He held posts at Shuchiin, Kyoto, Tokai, Hiroshima (1974–1986), and Kindai University (~1985–1993).
